rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
A potato is a stem tuber because it has buds. A sweet potato is a storage root. A thorn of a citrus-type stem is a modified stem, while a prickle may be superficial. The presence of nodes or buds decides a stem.
Racemose inflorescences open from below upward. Cymose ones open the top flower first. A flower is hypogynous when the ovary sits above the other parts, and the fruit is the ripened ovary, with a pericarp around the…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Leaflet axil vs stem axil:** only the compound leaf's rachis has an axillary bud; individual leaflets never do — the surest simple-vs-compound test.  ·  **Rhizome vs tuber:** rhizome is a horizontal stem with nodes/internodes (ginger); tuber is a swollen stem tip with "eyes" (potato).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Bud test for stem nature:** any flattened/spiny/root-like organ with nodes and buds is a modified stem.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Roots: tap (dicot) vs fibrous (monocot); modifications — storage, nodulated (Rhizobium), prop (banyan), stilt (maize), pneumatophores (Avicennia).  ·  Stems: nodes/buds always present; underground (tuber, rhizome, corm, bulb), aerial (tendril, thorn, phylloclade), sub-aerial (runner, stolon, offset, sucker).  ·  Leaves: base+petiole+lamina; reticulate (dicot) vs parallel (monocot) venation; simple vs compound (pinnate/palmate); phyllotaxy; modifications — tendril, spine, pitcher.  ·  Inflorescence: racemose (indefinite, acropetal — raceme, spike, umbel, head) vs cymose (definite, basipetal).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Caryopsis (grass fruit) fuses pericarp and seed coat — the world's staple "seeds" (wheat, rice, maize) are actually fruits.

rows.text: ***Opuntia phylloclade*** — flattened green stem doing photosynthesis; leaves reduced to spines.  ·  ***Sunflower head*** — racemose inflorescence compressed into a receptacle with ray and disc florets.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Flower: calyx, corolla, androecium, gynoecium; actinomorphic vs zygomorphic; hypogynous/perigynous/epigynous; placentation types.  ·  Fruits: simple fleshy (drupe — mango; berry — tomato), simple dry (legume — pea; caryopsis — wheat; achene, nut, capsule), aggregate (custard apple), multiple (pineapple).  ·  Dicot vs monocot: two vs one cotyledon, tap vs fibrous root, reticulate vs parallel venation, tetra/pentamerous vs trimerous flowers.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Thorn vs prickle:** thorn is a modified stem with vascular connection (deep-seated); prickles are superficial outgrowths (rose) removable without tearing.  ·  **Fruit vs seed:** fruit = fertilised ovary (+ accessories); seed = fertilised ovule. Wheat grain = caryopsis fruit, not a bare seed.  ·  ***Mango drupe*** — fleshy mesocarp + stony endocarp around the seed.
